fixes.explanation: Frogs, gnats and flies show up in the plagues on Egypt (Exodus 8:6, 17, 24). This verse is a different list. The LORD says, “I will send against them sword and famine and plague…” (Jeremiah 29:17).

Tribute never comes up in these verses. The LORD gives one reason, and it's about His words: “…they have not listened to My words, declares the LORD…” (Jeremiah 29:19). Sometimes our guesses jump ahead of the text.

Priests do show up later in this passage, but not here. In verse 19 the LORD says He sent His words “…again and again through My servants the prophets.” (Jeremiah 29:19). The word you want is prophets. Close, friend.

The verse doesn't say that. Right after naming the people in Jerusalem, the LORD says, “And neither have you exiles listened, declares the LORD.” (Jeremiah 29:19). The exiles are in the same boat on this one.
That's him. The LORD says He will deliver them to “…Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon…” (Jeremiah 29:21). The LORD says it plainly, so we'll say it plainly too.
That's what the LORD says. “In your own name you have sent out letters…” (Jeremiah 29:25). Shemaiah sent them in his own name, and I'd say that matters a lot.
No king is named as the sender in this verse. The LORD says, “In your own name you have sent out letters…” (Jeremiah 29:25). The name on this one is Shemaiah's own.

Yes, Jeremiah. Shemaiah writes, “So now, why have you not rebuked Jeremiah of Anathoth, who poses as a prophet among you?” (Jeremiah 29:27). Shemaiah says Jeremiah has sent word to the exiles in Babylon (Jeremiah 29:28). Complaining about him is a bold move.

Lengthy, that's it. Shemaiah complains that Jeremiah's message was, “Since the exile will be lengthy, build houses and settle down; plant gardens and eat their produce.” (Jeremiah 29:28). The message is about settling in, with houses, gardens and produce.

The LORD says the opposite. He says Shemaiah “…has prophesied to you—though I did not send him…” (Jeremiah 29:31). Shemaiah spoke, but the LORD didn't send him. The LORD also says Shemaiah “…has made you trust in a lie…” (Jeremiah 29:31).
Yes. The LORD says Shemaiah “…has made you trust in a lie…” (Jeremiah 29:31). The exiles are the ones he made do it. I think it's a sad line, because trust is a big thing to hand to the wrong voice.

That's the reason the verse ends on. The LORD says, “…for he has preached rebellion against the LORD.” (Jeremiah 29:32). The verse before adds that Shemaiah prophesied though the LORD did not send him, and made the exiles trust in a lie (Jeremiah 29:31). It's a heavy verse, and it's a good reminder of how much words can weigh.

No stealing is mentioned in these verses. The LORD says, “…for he has preached rebellion against the LORD.” (Jeremiah 29:32). Shemaiah's trouble is in what he preached. The LORD also says he prophesied though he was not sent, and made the exiles trust in a lie (Jeremiah 29:31).
